# Technical documentation {#c07-technical}

The main guide is organised around the tasks a researcher needs to complete:

```text
get data
   ↓
understand the files
   ↓
prepare the data
   ↓
specify the survey design
   ↓
analyse
```

This final chapter documents what happens under the hood. It is intended for researchers who need to understand exactly how AFLEARN variables were constructed; analysts adapting the harmonisation to additional MICS6 surveys; reviewers checking reproducibility; maintainers updating the processing scripts; and users who encounter a country-specific coding issue.

You do not need to read every page here before using the harmonised datasets.

| Page | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [FS harmonisation methods](#c07-fs-harmonisation) | How the non-reading selected-child variables are standardised |
| [Reading-variable construction](#c07-reading-construction) | How passages, scores, accuracy, comprehension and `reading_status` are constructed |
| [Country-specific issues](#c07-country-issues) | Survey-specific exceptions, repairs and comparability cautions |
| [Variable crosswalks and dictionaries](#c07-crosswalks) | How to trace every harmonised variable back to its source |
| [Why current_grade is not the child's grade](#c07-current-grade) | Why grade restarts within education levels and how to construct an administrative grade |
| [Validation and reproducibility](#c07-validation) | Checks that should be run whenever the harmonisation is changed |

AFLEARN keeps reading separate from the broader selected-child file.

```text
UNICEF fs.sav
      │
      ├───────────────────────────────┐
      │                               │
      ▼                               ▼
FS/background harmonisation      reading harmonisation
      │                               │
      ▼                               ▼
mics6-fs-harmonised             mics6-reading-harmonised
      │                               │
      └──────────────┬────────────────┘
                     ▼
                analysis file
```

This separation is useful because reading requires much more country- and passage-specific processing than most other FS variables.

The current processing scripts live in `Script/`:

```text
Script/harmonize-mics-fs-v1.0.R
Script/harmonize-mics-reading-v1.1.R
```

Both read the survey folders in `Data/UNICEF/` and write to `Data/AFLEARN Harmonised Data/`. The FS script produces `mics6-fs-harmonised.dta`, `mics6-fs-harmonised.rds` and `mics6_fs_variable_crosswalk.xlsx`. The reading script produces `mics6-reading-harmonised.dta` and `.rds`.

The current scripts recognise these 18 country codes:

```text
BEN CAF COD COM GHA GMB GNB LSO MDG MWI NGA
SLE STP SWZ TCD TGO TUN ZWE
```

Tunisia appears in more than one survey year in the current processing system.

A new survey should never simply be added to the supported list and assumed to work. It should first pass the validation process described at the end of this chapter.

The harmonised file should never be the only record of a coding decision. A substantive decision should appear in at least one of the processing script, the crosswalk, the country notes or the validation record, and ideally in more than one.

The purpose of this chapter is to make those decisions inspectable without forcing every user to read the entire R source code.
